section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a public highway?
options: a:45 mph.,b:30 mph.,c:55 mph.
note: On public highways, the maximum speed limit is 55 mph unless a different limit is posted. Always obey posted limits.

question: What is the first thing you should adjust when getting into a car to drive?
options: a:The steering wheel first.,b:The radio.,c:Your rearview mirror only.,d:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls comfortably.
note: Adjust your seat so you can see the road and reach controls, then adjust mirrors and steering wheel while seated in the proper position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,b:Drive out quickly to merge smoothly.,c:Blow your horn to warn approaching drivers.
note: When entering from a driveway or private road, you must yield to traffic and pedestrians on the roadway before proceeding.

question: Which of the following can cause distracted driving?
options: a:None of the above.,b:Only changing a radio station.,c:Talking or texting on a cell phone.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving, such as using a phone or handling food.

question: Are small children safe if held by an adult in a vehicle during a crash?
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:Will be protected only when properly secured in child restraints.,c:Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child seats or safety belts; no adult can reliably hold a child safe during a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the left.,b:The vehicle approaching from the right.,c:The larger vehicle.,d:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At an intersection of two similar roads without signs or signals, drivers must yield to vehicles approaching from the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,c:The speed at which you drive does not affect safety.
note: Driving excessively slowly can be hazardous by disrupting traffic flow and causing unsafe passing maneuvers; drive with the flow within speed limits.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a turn signal indicate?
options: a:Means drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,b:Is never used as a traffic signal.,c:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
note: A solid yellow arrow functions like a circular yellow light—slow and prepare to stop because the protected turn is ending.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Slow down and allow the other driver to safely return to the drive lane.,b:Accelerate to prevent them from passing.,c:Pull off the road immediately.,d:Honk to express disapproval.
note: Allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane when safe by slowing if necessary; avoid actions that create hazards.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle nearby, what should you expect?
options: a:That beeping your horn will improve safety.,b:The unexpected—children may swerve or make sudden moves.,c:That the child will be in total control.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; expect sudden movements and give extra space and caution.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you lawfully park?
options: a:You may not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:You may not park within 25 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:You may not park within 50 feet of a fire hydrant.
note: Parking within 50 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited to ensure emergency access.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: If your view is blocked, come to a stop and inch forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is accurate?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,d:All of the above.
note: You must obey crossing devices and flaggers, exercise caution at crossings without gates or lights, and never go around lowered gates.

question: Who benefits most from wearing seat belts?
options: a:All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.,b:The person driving the car.,c:Passengers when they are on a long drive.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant wears one; unbelted passengers become dangerous projectiles in crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for police vehicles first.,b:Maintain your normal driving speed and turn.,c:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.
note: You may turn right on a green light unless posted otherwise, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,d:Speed up to pass before they finish.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even when there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them cross safely.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,b:Assume it is safe to proceed after the first train passes.,c:Always stop before crossing any set of tracks.
note: When multiple tracks are present, wait until you're sure no other train is approaching on the other track before crossing.

question: What documents should a driver be ready to present during a traffic stop or equipment check?
options: a:Only proof of insurance.,b:Only the vehicle registration.,c:Driver's license
note: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must present their license, registration, and evidence of insurance upon request.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving distracting?
options: a:It is costly.,b:It distracts other drivers.,c:It improves attention to traffic.,d:It occupies the driver's hands
note: Using a phone takes your hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your attention away from driving tasks; it increases crash risk.

question: HOV lanes are reserved primarily for:
options: a:Only government vehicles.,b:Emergency vehicles exclusively.,c:Vehicles with the required number of occupants (high-occupancy vehicles).,d:Single-occupant vehicles at all times.
note: HOV lanes are for vehicles meeting the occupancy requirement shown on signs; motorcycles and certain other vehicles may also be allowed.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what is the proper procedure?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
note: Remain in your vehicle with your hands visible and wait for the officer to approach; retrieve license and registration when asked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.,b:Always stop at the end of the ramp before merging.,c:Yield only if the other vehicle signals.,d:Enter without checking mirrors.
note: Use the entrance ramp to gain speed and match freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles on the freeway.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow on a signal tell drivers?
options: a:Drivers may turn without yielding.,b:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,c:The protected left turn is about to end.
note: A yellow arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending; drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic as protection ends.

question: Which is NOT a recommended practice for safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware tinted windows reduce night visibility.,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
note: Carrying a flashlight is helpful, but it doesn't directly improve driving safety; keeping windshields clean and being aware of visibility limits are key.

question: In rainy weather, when is turning or stopping most hazardous?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: The first half hour of rain is especially hazardous because oil residues on the pavement can make the road slippery.

question: If you plan to pass a pedestrian on the roadway but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Maintain your speed and pass quickly.,c:Honk to make the pedestrian move over.,d:Pass the pedestrian before the oncoming vehicle arrives.
note: When faced with multiple hazards, handle one at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if safe.

question: When should you use low-beam headlights?
options: a:On a well-lit street at night.,b:Only when an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on.,c:In fog
note: Use low beams in foggy or precipitation conditions to reduce glare and improve visibility; high beams can reflect and worsen visibility in these conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign—come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They require wider turns and need more stopping distance.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,d:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks need longer distances to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed; they also require wider turning space.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do before moving over?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Glance over your shoulder and signal at least 100 feet in residential areas.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and signal early (about 100 feet in residential areas) before changing lanes.

question: What is the usual effect of driving while distracted by other activities?
options: a:It is never dangerous.,b:It makes drivers faster to respond.,c:Drivers react more slowly to hazards.
note: Distractions slow reaction times and reduce awareness, increasing the likelihood of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do functioning brake lights tell other drivers?
options: a:Are changing lanes.,b:Are making a turn.,c:Have your emergency brake on.,d:Are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping. Keep them working properly at all times.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what is the hand signal indicating?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Slow down only.,d:Stop.
note: A left arm pointed downward indicates the driver intends to stop or slow significantly. Be prepared to adjust your driving.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,d:Only before passing.
note: Frequently check mirrors to remain aware of traffic around your vehicle; avoid developing a fixed stare ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do on a green arrow signal?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.,b:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the direction shown after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which passing actions are unlawful?
options: a:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Both of the above.,c:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone.
note: It is illegal to cross the centerline to pass in no-passing zones, near hills and curves where sight distance is limited, at street and railroad crossings, or where signs or solid yellow lines prohibit passing.

question: When should you reduce your speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Never; always follow the posted limit.,b:Whenever conditions require it,c:Only when police direct you to do so.
note: Posted speed limits apply to ideal conditions; reduce speed when weather, visibility, or road conditions make it unsafe to drive at the limit.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.,b:Because you will be caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:Because it will save fuel.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead and have larger blind spots; increasing following distance improves visibility and safety.

question: How should you expect children to behave when driving in areas where they play?
options: a:To stop at the curb before crossing.,b:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,c:To run out in front of you without looking.
note: Children may not understand traffic danger and can suddenly run into the roadway; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: What is the correct response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid heavy braking until the vehicle has slowed.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator and slow gradually; avoid heavy braking until the car has slowed considerably.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and discourage lane changes; passing is not allowed.

question: To reduce headlight glare at night from oncoming vehicles, where should you look?
options: a:At the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,c:Straight at the headlights.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right roadside to reduce glare while maintaining lane position.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your high beams repeatedly.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull alongside and yell at the driver.
note: To avoid escalation and road rage, remain calm, let it go, and maintain safe control of your vehicle.

question: After a train has passed at a crossing, what should you do before driving on?
options: a:Drive immediately if the first train is clear.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.,d:Do both — look for another train and wait until signals stop.
note: Even after one train passes, always watch for another approaching on any track. Do not proceed until all gates are raised and all warning signals have stopped flashing.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Shift into neutral to coast through the water.,b:Maintain posted speed to get through quickly.,c:Avoid it if possible or drive slowly through shallow water
note: Avoid deep puddles when possible; drive slowly through standing water and avoid sudden maneuvers to reduce the risk of skidding or hydroplaning.

question: What is important to remember about wet pavement and the start of rain?
options: a:You need less stopping distance when wet.,b:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.,c:Roads are especially slippery just after it starts to rain.
note: Immediately after rain begins, oil and dirt mix with water creating a slippery film; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: If you are involved in an accident, which action is appropriate?
options: a:Stop and move your vehicle out of traffic if possible,b:Drive to the nearest hospital immediately if anyone is injured.,c:Leave the scene if damage is minor.,d:Call the police without stopping.
note: If involved in a crash stop immediately, move your vehicle out of the roadway when possible, help the injured, and call law enforcement or emergency services if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Select a safe gap and merge into traffic.
note: Find a gap large enough to safely enter traffic and merge smoothly from the entrance ramp without stopping unless absolutely necessary.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the steering wheel sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Apply the brakes hard and then steer quickly.,d:Accelerate to regain pavement.
note: If you run off the roadway, stay calm: hold the wheel, ease off the gas, gently brake, and when safe, look for a place to re-enter traffic gradually.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly both directions.,b:Never; it is illegal to drive around lowered gates.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: You must not go around or under lowered railroad crossing gates; wait until the gates are fully raised and it is safe to cross.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:The driver should honk their horn.,b:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,c:No special action is required.
note: Be cautious when encountering animals; slow down and pass slowly to avoid startling them and causing an accident.

question: If you pass your interstate exit, the correct action is to:
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.,d:Make a U-turn through the median.
note: Do not stop, back up, or attempt unsafe turns on the interstate. Continue to the next exit and re-route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck will always match posted speed,b:You may not be able to legally pass only if signs say so.,c:The truck may travel slower than the posted speed limit
note: Large vehicles often slow on steep grades; be cautious when approaching or attempting to pass, especially where visibility is limited.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When driving more slowly than the posted limit.,c:When you are being tailgated.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space ahead to avoid sudden braking; slow gradually or change lanes to reduce risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit shows the maximum legal speed for ideal road and weather conditions; adjust speed downward when conditions are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at an upcoming corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:All approaching vehicles and pedestrians with the right-of-way.,b:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a 'Walk' signal.,c:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and others who have the right-of-way before making a left turn.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
options: a:50 feet,b:10 feet,c:25 feet
note: You cannot park within 25 feet of a crosswalk or intersection to ensure pedestrian safety and visibility.

question: What should you do to reduce the chance of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as in dry conditions.,b:Slow down and drive more slowly than in ideal conditions.,c:Drive through deep water at higher speed.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose contact with the road in wet conditions; reducing speed lowers that risk.

question: What does a solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the roadway indicate?
options: a:An intersection is just ahead.,b:A mandatory left turn ahead.,c:The road narrows ahead.
note: If the edge line slants toward the center, that signals the traveled roadway is narrowing ahead; adjust your position and speed accordingly.

question: Double solid yellow center lines on the roadway indicate:
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:No passing is permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited in both directions except to turn into driveways or make permitted left turns.

question: You should not enter railroad tracks unless you can clear them completely so your entire vehicle fits on the far side:
options: a:Only when lights are flashing,b:True,c:False,d:Only at marked crossings
note: Never cross railroad tracks unless there is room on the other side for your entire vehicle; stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They do not need extra room to maneuver.
note: Trucks have extensive blind spots and need more distance to stop and maneuver; avoid lingering near them.

question: When the center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, it means:
options: a:You must always stay in your lane.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You may only make right turns from this lane.,d:You are in a passing zone and may pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means you may cross to pass, while a solid yellow line beside your lane means passing is prohibited from your side.

question: When preparing to pass a motorcycle, what must you do regarding lane position?
options: a:Stay in the right lane and crowd the motorcycle.,b:Blow your horn to force the motorcycle onto the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane when passing and allow a full lane width to the motorcycle.
note: When passing a motorcycle, give a full lane width and do not share a lane with the rider; ensure you complete the pass safely before returning to your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you near an intersection, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Brake sharply in the center of the intersection.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red—slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With Anti-Lock Braking Systems, press and hold the brake firmly; the ABS will modulate braking for you.

question: At what speed should you travel relative to others on the road?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: Drive at a speed that's safe for current road and weather conditions, never exceeding the legal limit.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,b:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
note: Split the difference—steer a middle course to maximize clearance from the parked cars while avoiding oncoming traffic.

question: Orange-colored roadway signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:Work zones.,c:School zones.
note: Orange signs typically warn of construction or maintenance work zones; proceed with caution.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed carefully; you do not need to come to a complete stop unless required by other signs or conditions.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street rather than in a crosswalk, you:
options: a:May proceed without yielding.,b:Can speed up to pass before they reach your lane.,c:Must stop for them.,d:Should honk to make them move.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing outside a crosswalk.

question: Highway signs that warn of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Guide signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Warning signs.,d:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead that may require caution (curves, intersections, narrow bridges, etc.).

question: When should you drive in a reversible lane that displays a red X above it?
options: a:When there is no visible oncoming traffic.,b:Never.,c:Only during rush hour.,d:To pass a slow vehicle
note: A red X indicates the lane is closed to your direction of travel; never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for:
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,d:Larger vehicles can stop quicker in emergencies.
note: Large trucks require greater stopping distances and make wider turns; give them extra space and avoid locations where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection requires the same action as what sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means stop and proceed only after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, like a stop sign.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway where you are driving, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Slow down and pass with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Continue at the same speed.
note: When pedestrians are close to the road, reduce speed and be prepared to stop. Children and others may step into the roadway unexpectedly.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them?
options: a:False — they have small blind spots.,b:True — they can have blind spots that extend far behind.
note: Large vehicles can have extensive blind spots, so do not follow too closely behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right first.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of the space you want to occupy.,c:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately.
note: Begin parallel parking by stopping even with the vehicle ahead of the empty space, then back in while steering appropriately.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering control.,b:Faster stopping without skidding.,c:Prevention of brake freezing.
note: Hard braking on icy or snowy surfaces can lock the wheels, causing loss of steering; maintain slow, controlled speeds to avoid this.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you get into the car.,b:Before you start driving.,c:Whenever you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust mirrors, seats, and secure items before driving; do not wait until the vehicle is moving to make adjustments.

question: If it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Turn off headlights to prevent glare.,b:Slow down.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,d:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
note: Reduce speed, turn on headlights, and increase following distance in rain. If visibility is severely reduced, pull over safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light requires you to:
options: a:Ignore it if no other vehicles are present.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Stop and treat the intersection like a stop sign.,d:Slow down and proceed if clear.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign — come to a full stop and continue only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a turn lane to turn left and there is oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: When preparing to turn left, signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep wheels pointed straight until you begin turning.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim their high beams, where should you focus?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, glance toward the right side of the road to reduce glare and maintain course.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Alerts drivers to school zones.,b:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of existing or potential roadway hazards and conditions ahead.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain speed and stay in your lane.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road, stop, and remain stopped until it has passed.

question: How can you reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road and then resume forward scanning.,b:Stare at the centerline of the road.,c:Turn on your high beams to counter glare.
note: If oncoming headlights are blinding, glance briefly to the right edge of the road to avoid direct glare and maintain control.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.,b:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,c:Ensure your tires are properly inflated.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, keep tires properly inflated with good tread and reduce speed in wet conditions.

question: What is the best way to ensure safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,c:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
note: Before backing, walk to the rear of your vehicle to look for children or obstacles; mirrors alone may not reveal hazards.

question: Which practice is recommended on slippery surfaces like snow or ice?
options: a:Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.,b:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.,c:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.
note: Use a low gear going down steep hills and increase following distance; unless ABS-equipped, pump brakes gently to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to stop in a travel lane to let a passenger out?
options: a:True — you may stop if necessary.,b:False — you must not stop in travel lanes to let out passengers.
note: Do not stop in travel lanes for letting passengers out; continue to a safe pull-off area.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck (no gates or flashing lights), you should:
options: a:Turn your radio down and proceed at usual speed.,b:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,c:Proceed without stopping if no lights are flashing.,d:Only continue once cleared by a flagger.
note: At crossings without active signals, slow down, look and listen for trains from both directions, and cross only when it is safe.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Drive at a reduced speed until destination.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue.,d:Open a window and keep driving.
note: To avoid the dangers of drowsy driving, stop and rest or switch drivers. Short breaks and shared driving are safer than trying to push through fatigue.

question: What does a green arrow lane-use signal above a lane mean?
options: a:You must use this lane only to make a left turn.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:You may drive in that lane normally (lane is open).
note: A green arrow over a lane indicates the lane is open for travel in the direction shown; lane control signals manage direction of flow.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:Less dangerous because traffic is lighter.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous due to reduced visibility and increased chance of impaired or tired drivers.
note: Night driving is more hazardous because it is harder to see, headlights can cause glare, and more drivers may be tired or impaired.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling over and stopping when safe.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass by crossing the lines.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:The right lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Yield.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Honk to let them know you’re there.
note: Yield to a transit vehicle signaling to re-enter traffic so it can safely merge back into the roadway.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what is the safe action?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
note: Do not try to turn between a large vehicle and the curb; wait until it has completed its turn to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you should:
options: a:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.,b:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Signal only after passing.,d:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
note: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and signaling has been used.

question: Which statement about changing weather is true?
options: a:You should always maintain the same speed regardless of rain or fog.,b:A sudden change in weather requires you to adjust your driving.,c:Weather does not affect stopping distance.,d:Ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: When weather changes suddenly, reduce speed and adapt your driving; slow down in rain and fog and be aware of drivers behind you.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you feel your tires losing contact (hydroplaning), ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until traction returns.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Interior dome lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Use a turn signal to indicate your intention.,b:Look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.,d:Fail to check your side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic.
note: Do not change lanes without first checking mirrors, signaling, and checking blind spots — failing to check mirrors is what you should not do.

question: Before turning on the ignition you should:
options: a:Buckle your own safety belt and make sure passengers are belted.,b:Make sure your radio is off.,c:Check your engine oil level.,d:Close all windows.
note: Always fasten your seat belt before driving and ensure passengers are also buckled; it is illegal in New Mexico to drive unbelted.

question: Signs colored orange normally indicate:
options: a:Regulatory requirements.,b:School zone warnings.,c:Work zones.
note: Orange signs are used in work zones to warn drivers of road work or maintenance ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you cannot pass safely unless:
options: a:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,b:You can clearly see the road ahead and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle can reach the speed needed to pass safely.,d:All of the above.
note: You must be able to see clearly ahead, be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have sufficient vehicle capability to pass safely.

question: For a driver aged 21 or older, what BAC is illegal to drive at or above?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older, operating a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher is illegal.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what else should occupants do?
options: a:Disable the airbags for safety.,b:Sit as far forward as possible.,c:Seat belts are not necessary.,d:Always wear seat belts as well.
note: Airbags are supplemental restraint systems and must be used in combination with lap and shoulder belts for best protection.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary.,b:Keep driving normally if other lanes are available.,c:Stop immediately in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, yield by slowing and pulling over to provide a clear route; do not try to outdrive it.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, what should drivers do?
options: a:Maintain speed and stay in the lane.,b:Pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass.,c:Stop in the intersection until it passes.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren, pull to the right side of the road and allow it to pass.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, drivers adjacent to the dashed line may pass; those next to the solid may not.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when safe; a solid next to you means you may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Only stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light is green unless turning on red is permitted and safe.,c:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present.,d:Continue because they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady red signal requires a complete stop. Right turns on red are permitted only where allowed and after stopping and yielding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way because the vehicle to your right goes first.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; if that vehicle is to your right then you go first.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that a ____ light is about to appear.
options: a:Steady green,b:Steady red,c:Flashing yellow,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to change to a steady red light — prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn to warn them.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles caught in the intersection; stop and let them clear the intersection safely.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Are better drivers because they're more cautious.,d:Should drive only in familiar areas.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination; it is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who must you yield to?
options: a:Drivers who arrived after you.,b:Drivers who signal first.,c:Drivers who arrived before you.
note: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to the vehicles that arrived before you and proceed in turn.

question: What's the key point about speed management in curves?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter and slow at the sharpest part.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
note: Because inertia can push your vehicle outward in a curve, slow down before entering the curve to maintain control.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a:You may proceed in any direction slowly.,b:You may turn only in the direction of the green arrow (after yielding as required).,c:You may go straight only.,d:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
note: When a green arrow is displayed along with a red light, you may turn in the arrow's direction; you may not go straight or turn another direction.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Come to an immediate complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of potential hazards; reduce speed and cross with caution.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what is the proper action?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,c:Speed up to get out of the way in the next block.
note: Move to the right curb and stop to allow the emergency vehicle a clear path; if in an intersection, clear it first then pull over.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to get attention while stopped in the lane.,b:Pull off the roadway,c:Get out and wave down passing cars.
note: If you stop on the shoulder of an interstate, use your emergency flashers and remain in the vehicle if safe; walking along high-speed roads is dangerous.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check blind spots?
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Turning left or right.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder when you intend to change lanes; you should also check when turning or maneuvering near curbs.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop even without a stop sign present.,b:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when children are nearby.
note: Yield to pedestrians in or about to enter crosswalks and be especially alert when approaching school crossing signs.

question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:After changing lanes.,c:Early enough (about 100 feet) before you change lanes to pass.
note: Signal early so other drivers understand your intentions and have time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:All of the above.,d:Sound your horn before moving.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before any lateral movement.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow and white,c:Yellow
note: Yellow lines down the center separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Yes — if you are sitting in the back seat.,b:Yes — if you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.,c:No — it is illegal to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages on a public highway.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an alcoholic beverage while on a public road or sidewalk. Keeping an open container in areas normally occupied by the driver or passenger is prohibited on any public road.

question: At a red light that shows a green arrow for your direction, when may you proceed?
options: a:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only after the green arrow changes to a solid green.
note: If you are in the lane corresponding to a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction when the way is clear.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your right foot for both acceleration and braking.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Use whichever foot feels comfortable, even the left.,d:Use both feet simultaneously for better control.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake; using the left foot for braking can cause confusion and unsafe inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and enter only after you've identified a safe gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and then speed up.,c:Use the shoulder to reach traffic speed.
note: On short ramps without acceleration lanes, wait for a safe gap before accelerating onto the interstate; often you'll be stopped until a gap appears.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through the zone quickly.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Maintain your normal speed through the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted work zone signs, and be prepared to stop; road workers may be near the traffic lanes.

question: Holding a driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Right that cannot be revoked.,b:Requirement you must carry at all times.,c:Permanent entitlement.,d:Privilege
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and can be suspended or revoked if you abuse it or violate laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to enter a gap in highway traffic?
options: a:Check behind you and to the sides, then watch the vehicle ahead before merging.,b:Speed up and expect other drivers to make room.,c:Rely only on vehicles behind the gap.
note: Before changing lanes or merging, check for traffic to the sides and rear and ensure there is sufficient space to enter safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with blocked view from oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Rely on another driver to wave you through.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane clears.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before completing the turn.
note: Do not start a left turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic and safe to enter.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct first action?
options: a:Brake hard immediately and turn sharply.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: In a blowout, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually before steering off the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:Any speed below the limit regardless of conditions.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions.,c:The posted maximum speed only.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the area and current conditions, not merely at or below the posted limit.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, prescription or over-the-counter medications, and lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal or illegal drugs, and fatigue; all can reduce perception, judgment, and reaction time.

question: True or false: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your chance of a crash.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only if using hands-free,d:Only when driving under 25 mph.
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction and increases crash risk. Even hands-free use can divert attention from driving.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you expect?
options: a:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.,b:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,c:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
note: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars because doors or people may suddenly appear into your lane.

question: Like alcohol or drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability.,b:It improves attention.,c:It can impair your judgment and slow reaction time.
note: Drowsiness reduces awareness, slows reactions, and impairs judgment—effects similar to impairment from alcohol or drugs.

question: What is the only medically proven method to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Give your body time.,c:Exercise vigorously.,d:Drink coffee.
note: Alcohol leaves the body only with time. Other measures do not reduce BAC or speed recovery.

question: When passing large vehicles you should be careful because:
options: a:They always signal before changing lanes.,b:They cannot be passed on the highway.,c:They have large blind spots and you should avoid driving beside them for long periods.,d:They always travel slower than traffic.
note: Large trucks and buses have significant blind spots; do not remain beside them — either pass quickly or drop back.

question: How can you avoid loss of traction (hydroplaning) on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Drive with your parking lights on.,c:Slow down.,d:Apply the brakes firmly and suddenly.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions and maintain tires in good condition; if traction is lost, take foot off the gas and steer straight until control returns.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a child who is about to run into the street.,b:When passing a bicyclist.,c:While traveling through an intersection to hurry traffic.,d:To express frustration at another driver.
note: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you and immediate attention is needed — for example, if a child is about to enter the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road, when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you provide?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Demand the other driver move over.,c:Allow at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.
note: On narrow roads, both vehicles must leave at least half of the main-traveled portion of the road to safely pass each other.

question: When driving in rain, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights only.,b:Use parking lights only.,c:Use low beam headlights.,d:Use high beam headlights.
note: In rain, use your low beam headlights so others can see your vehicle. High beams may reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: Which effects can alcoholic beverages have on a driver?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking, and give a false sense of confidence.,b:They always improve coordination.,c:They have no impact on judgment.
note: Alcohol dulls judgment, slows reactions, impairs coordination and vision, and can produce a false sense of confidence, making driving unsafe.

question: If you are sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you allow it?
options: a:Driving on the shoulder beside you.,b:Use of only half a lane.,c:Use of a full traffic lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles for legal purposes; allow them a full lane width for safe maneuvering.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Keeping eye contact during a conversation with a passenger.,b:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,c:Focusing only on the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Avoid distractions such as daydreaming, looking at passengers, or reading while driving; continually scan the road and mirrors.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:It is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:It is a school bus.,c:It indicates a vehicle carrying hazardous materials.,d:It is an ambulance.
note: An orange reflective triangle means the vehicle is traveling at speeds under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

question: Which devices are commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper turning lanes?
options: a:Lane arrows and pavement markings indicating turning lanes.,b:Flashing red lights only.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows on signs and pavement are used to indicate which lanes are intended for specific turning or through movements.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing the street.,c:Continue ahead—the motorist has the right-of-way.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians within a crosswalk and wait until the crossing is clear before proceeding.

question: When a curb is painted which color, it usually indicates a loading zone or parking restriction?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Yellow
note: Painted curbs specify parking restrictions; a yellow curb often marks a loading zone or other temporary/no parking area.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Increase following distance later.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Reduce your speed.,d:Turn on interior lights.
note: When visibility decreases, slow down first so you have more time to react to hazards; then use lights and wipers as needed.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up as he or she is passing you.,b:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.,c:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.
note: If someone drives aggressively behind you, safely move out of their way and avoid eye contact or escalating actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing and signaling?
options: a:You only need to signal at any time.,b:Return to your lane before you can see the passed car in your rearview mirror.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before passing, signal early (about 100 feet), check mirrors and blind spots, and return to the lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
options: a:More coordinated.,b:More intoxicated.,c:Less affected.,d:More sober.
note: Higher BAC means greater impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: Emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights:
options: a:Do not need to be given any special consideration.,b:May not use loudspeakers for instructions.,c:May be passed quickly by other drivers.,d:Have the right-of-way; you must yield and follow any instructions given by their loudspeaker.
note: Yield immediately to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens, and obey any directions delivered via loudspeaker.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way when they are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,b:Anyone in a marked or unmarked crosswalk or intersection.,c:Only pedestrians crossing at intersections with signals.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk and exercise caution for anyone crossing the street.

question: What must you do when you encounter lowered gates and flashing lights at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised and the tracks are clear.,b:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Slowly drive under the gate if no train is visible.
note: It is illegal and dangerous to drive around lowered crossing gates; stop and wait until the gates are fully raised and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto interstate traffic, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the lane to be completely clear before merging.,b:Merge carefully into the gap when safe.,c:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.
note: Accelerate to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into an identified gap when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you drive on the right shoulder of the road?
options: a:When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.,b:When the car in front of you is turning.,c:Only when told to do so by an official.
note: You may only drive on the shoulder when directed by an official; do not use shoulders to pass other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when:
options: a:You are on a hill or curve with limited visibility.,b:There is a solid line next to your lane indicating no passing.,c:You are in a lane next to a broken line and it is safe to do so.,d:You cannot see ahead clearly.
note: You may pass when the line next to your lane is broken and the way ahead is clear; never pass where lines indicate you may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:On a straight roadway with clear view for 500 feet.,b:Where a sign specifically allows U-turns.,c:On or near any curve or hill where you cannot be seen by others.,d:In a parking lot.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where oncoming traffic cannot see you in time to avoid a collision.

question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), should you quickly apply the brakes? True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not apply the brakes suddenly; instead, ease off the accelerator and steer gently until you regain traction.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery?
options: a:After several hours of steady rain.,b:Just after it begins to rain.,c:One to two hours after rain starts.
note: Roads are especially slick at the start of rainfall because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with water, producing a greasy film.

question: When driving on major highways, you should:
options: a:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead at all times.,b:Drive at a constant speed regardless of conditions.,c:Avoid changing lanes even if needed.,d:Stay alert and keep scanning the road for hazards.
note: Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be prepared to react to unexpected hazards to avoid highway hypnosis and collisions.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings inform drivers about lane positioning, passing zones, and upcoming roadway conditions.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:As a signal to speed up.,b:As a yield sign—slow but do not stop.,c:As a stop sign—come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red light means stop; treat it like a stop sign and go only when it is safe.

question: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median, what should drivers on your side do?
options: a:Stop until the bus's stop arm is lifted even on a divided highway.,b:Continue driving; you do not need to stop.,c:Stop until the bus begins moving.
note: On a highway divided by a median, drivers on the opposite side are not required to stop for a stopped bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Use high beams at all times to see better.,c:Keep instrument lighting bright to be seen by others.
note: At night you must drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limit driving to weekdays.,c:Drive slowly at all times.,d:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt is the most effective way to reduce injury or death in a vehicle crash.

question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Treat it like a red light.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,d:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution—slow down and watch for pedestrians and cross traffic.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light as you approach an intersection?
options: a:Stop completely before entering,b:Slow down and proceed with caution after checking for cross traffic.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and cross the intersection only when it is safe to do so.

question: If a vehicle with high beams approaches and does not dim them, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the centerline of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining enough view of the roadway.

question: Which steps help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:Allowing extra travel time.
note: To reduce aggressive driving, obey speed limits, signal properly, and plan extra time so you avoid rushing.

question: When you see a school crossing (pentagonal) sign, what should you do?
options: a:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether or not a stop sign is present.,c:Sound your horn to warn nearby children.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate school zones or crossings—slow down, watch for children, and be ready to stop.

question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,c:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the flagger's instructions.
note: Obey and follow directions from flaggers in construction zones; failing to do so is dangerous and illegal.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is true?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: Broken white centerlines indicate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: Where are stop lines painted across lanes?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines across lanes at intersections and crosswalks indicating where to stop your vehicle.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes mean?
options: a:You may only change lanes from the left lane.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; a dashed white line allows lane changes and passing when safe.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway.,c:Make a U-turn through the median.,d:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a freeway. Proceed to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: On the highway, regularly looking far ahead of your vehicle helps you to:
options: a:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Helps you keep up with traffic.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.,d:Makes lane changes unnecessary.
note: Watching far ahead reduces last-minute maneuvers, helps keep traffic flowing smoothly, and improves safety.

question: If a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload and its lights are flashing, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Slow and pass cautiously on the right.,c:Pass immediately on the left if no children are seen.,d:Proceed at reduced speed without stopping.
note: When a bus is stopped with red lights and stop arm out, all drivers in both directions on undivided roadways must stop until the signals are turned off.

question: Ramps and bridges often freeze before roadways do.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Because ramps and bridges are exposed to air on all sides, they can become icy before road surfaces and require extra caution in freezing weather.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:On the side with the lightest traffic.,b:On the same side as traffic flow.,c:On the side facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and motorists can see them.

question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or are crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Will drive no differently than when thinking clearly.,b:Should take time to calm down and focus before driving.,c:Can drive faster because senses are heightened.,d:Continue driving and hope feelings pass.
note: Emotional distress can distract you and impair driving. Take time to calm down and focus before getting behind the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your signal is green, what should you do?
options: a:Don't enter until you can get completely across.,b:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,c:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
note: Even on a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking intersections can lead to citations.

question: What does a \No passing zone\" sign tell drivers?"
options: a:It is not safe or legal to pass in the indicated area.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:To speed up slightly to pass other vehicles.,d:That passing is permitted during daylight only.
note: \No passing zone\" signs mark locations where passing is unsafe or illegal due to limited visibility or other hazards."

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a motorcycle in good weather.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view and when visibility or road conditions are poor.
note: Increase following distance when your view is obstructed by a large vehicle, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or if someone is tailgating you.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Because they don't follow traffic rules on purpose.,b:Because children are smaller,c:Because they can ride faster than adults.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give extra space and be especially cautious near schools and parks.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Continue at normal speed without looking for hazards.,d:Yield only to vehicles on your left.
note: Flashing yellow is a warning to use caution. Slow down, look, and proceed when safe.

question: What is a common risk of driving on worn or bald tires?
options: a:They are more likely to hydroplane.,b:They improve cornering control.,c:They reduce stopping distance.
note: Tires with little or no tread increase the risk of hydroplaning, reduce traction, and can make it harder to control or stop your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street in your direction of travel, where should you enter?
options: a:Into the lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:Always into the far left lane.,c:Into the lane marked by a painted arrow only.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, turn into the lane closest to your original lane and do not immediately change lanes.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:Proceed through the intersection if the road is clear (or turn if not prohibited),c:Always slow and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go through the intersection when it is safe; you must still yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Relax, concentrate on driving, and not take other drivers' actions personally.,b:Drive above posted speeds to keep traffic moving.,c:Tailgate slow drivers to prompt them to speed up.,d:Use your horn frequently to express displeasure.
note: Stay calm, be realistic about travel time, obey speed limits, and be forgiving of others to reduce the chance of aggressive driving.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, how should you respond?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and drive through the smoke.,b:Reduce speed,c:Turn on high-beam headlights and continue.
note: Heavy smoke can impair breathing and vision; slow down, move right, and stop in a safe location until it is clear to continue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do even if the light is green?
options: a:Turn left and find another route immediately.,b:Follow other vehicles into the intersection and wait there.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without stopping; blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At railroad crossings.,b:On hills and curves.,c:At intersections.
note: Passing is unsafe and unlawful on hills and curves, and it is also prohibited at intersections and railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to block an intersection?
options: a:Yes,b:Only during rush hour.,c:No — you must not enter unless you can clear the intersection.
note: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it without stopping in the intersection.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.,d:Ease off pedals and steer in the direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle skids, release the accelerator or brakes and steer into the skid to regain control. Do not brake hard or turn off the ignition.

question: If a transit (bus) signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, what is required of you?
options: a:Move to the left lane.,b:Honk to let them know you're there.,c:Yield to the transit vehicle.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter traffic so they can merge safely after loading or unloading passengers.

question: How can sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They only cause visibility problems.,b:They only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:They can cause problems for all vehicles
note: Strong wind gusts can affect the stability and control of any vehicle and may also reduce visibility by blowing dust or debris into the roadway.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:It causes pollution only.,b:It can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning.,c:It can cause a loss of hearing.
note: An exhaust leak can allow deadly carbon monoxide fumes into the passenger compartment; replace faulty parts promptly.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Reaction distance.,b:Steering ability.,c:Braking distance.
note: Perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance determine stopping distance; steering ability itself is not a direct component of stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing an intersection without traffic lights, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,b:Whoever started moving last must yield.,c:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic lights, whether or not a marked crosswalk is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When considering right-of-way, what is the safest assumption for a driver?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Rely solely on traffic signals to determine right-of-way.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,d:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Never assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Be prepared to yield if it will prevent a collision.

question: What is the typical shape and color of temporary construction/work zone signs?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black markings.,b:Round with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction or maintenance activities.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Pass on the right regardless of conditions.,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist then pass quickly.,c:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,d:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicycle, slow down and leave as much room as possible; bicyclists are vulnerable and may swerve to avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Turn either right or left because the road is blocked ahead.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,d:Stop completely
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a full stop. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear.

question: Excessive speed most often leads to what?
options: a:High-risk decision-making and increased crash risk.,b:No change in crash likelihood.,c:Improved ability to react to hazards.
